# Generated files

This map names the generated groups, their producers, their inputs, their consumers and
the check that covers each. It owns the generation rule; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` owns the
surrounding module boundaries.

## The rule

Every generated file is produced by one `make gen-<group>` rule and listed in the
Makefile's `GENERATED_PATHS`.
`make check-gen` regenerates the stale Lean-only groups.
It refuses changed committed files through `git diff --exit-code` over those paths.
`make -B gen` re-cuts every group, including the host-cut groups.
Then `make check-gen` checks the committed files.
A generated file names its producer: `GENERATED by <producer>; do not edit`.
JSON holds this line in its producer field.
A TSV projection keeps its column header first and inherits the producer of its companion JSON.
The build graph decides whether a producer must run. Drift is the diff.
The producers reached by `make check-full` hash source closures, inputs, outputs, package pins and tool identities.
Other producers retain their named prerequisites in the Makefile.
Until 2026-09-13, generated files recorded a Git revision and a fingerprint of the producer's import closure.
The header or a `.cut-from` sidecar held them, and a separate stamp gate checked them.
A core edit rewrote about three hundred labels per commit.
Four families sat outside the generation command.
A Lean edit failed the hermetic checks until someone ran the host commands in order.
Wave 1 removed the labels, sidecars, stamp gate and per-script result caches.
The Makefile holds the dependency graph.

The three tiers are:

- **build artifact**: produced by the build system or build setup and never committed;
- **committed projection**: generated output kept in Git and checked byte for byte
  against a fresh run;
- **vendored input**: copied from an identified source, with provenance recorded.

`make gen` runs every stale group of the Makefile's `GEN_GROUPS` (this file does not restate it).
Each group's marker depends on the markers of the groups whose outputs its producer reads. So a
regenerated group re-cuts the groups that read it, and no other (the codegen refactor's CR-2).
Every Lean producer reads the derived group's modules. The semantics report is no group:
`make gen-semantics` runs it on demand, and neither `make gen`, `make check-gen` nor any gate
waits on it (owner, 2026-10-18). Its committed projection is `generated/semantics.md` alone. The
report's JSON and its document's JSON stay under `.lake/gen/semantics-report`. One typed report
gives the report's JSON and one document (`tools/Tools/Document.lean`). The document gives the
Markdown and its own JSON, which the site splits into pages. Its refusal
controls are `make check-sweep`.
The fixtures group is hermetic in the same way. Its marker also depends on its own outputs,
because Lake does not take a file read by `include_str` as an input. A fixture that changes
alone is written again from Lean, and a committed fixture that Lean does not write is drift.
Its marker depends on every Lean source its writers import.
`scripts/lean-imports.py --closure` reads this import closure from the headers.
The marker does not wait for `build`.
When a program changes, the binding battery refuses the old fixture, and the default build is red
until `make gen-fixtures` writes the fixture again.
The group lcnf is another deliberate exception.
It sits in the order between derived and eff, because eff cuts the engine's layout mirror from
the api_engine.ml that lcnf writes.
Its marker is not a link of the hermetic chain, so `check-gen` does not reach it.
The OCaml lane does: `make check-ocaml` depends on the lcnf marker.
So a change of the machine re-cuts the generated engine before the lane builds it.
The group lcnf used to run last, after readme, which made `make gen` a non-fixpoint.
A changed row then needed a second pass before the mirror agreed with the face (tooling plan 4.2).
`make gen-<group>` regenerates one group, and `make clean-gen` forgets the markers.
The recipes hold the Lean lane one at a time.

## Generator bootstrap

`make gen-derived` can run before the Effect4 library builds.
Its freshness inputs include Lean source files and directories, package pins and declared producer inputs.
A missing derived output also triggers its producer.
The variance producer uses its own narrow build.
Neither producer first builds the whole library.

`Effect4Gen.Driver.sourceGraph` parses ordinary source imports with Lean's parser.
The manifest declares imports for generated modules, including missing outputs.
The scheduler includes each generator executable's imports and each manifest row's runtime imports.
It refuses missing import evidence, repeated output paths, self-dependencies and dependency cycles.
Each stage builds its prerequisites, generates temporary files, then compares or installs them.
A failed stage installs none of its outputs.
A difference in check mode stops generation before dependent stages build.
The final narrow build checks every generated Lean module.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[Source headers and manifest] --> P[Dependency stages]
  P --> E[Early generator]
  E --> F[Generated prerequisites]
  F --> C[Catalogue generator]
  C --> O[Dependent outputs]
  O --> B[Generated module builds]
```

## Program object codecs

The derived family's Object group owns `SigApp`, `Object`, `Certificate` and the two store read-refusal alphabets.
It imports the carriers, store readers and generated program/value codecs, without the printer.
Refusals depends on Object and adds `Object.LoadRefusal` after `AdmitRefusal`.
It also imports `Api.Session` and generates `SessionRefusal` after its component refusals.
Check imports Object's `SigApp` codec. Tool imports the revised `LiveRecord` carrier.
The manifest is the only list of these generated carriers.
Make reads its output paths directly, so a new group also enters freshness and drift checks.

## Declarations generated during Lean elaboration

The typed-state group has no generated source file or committed table. `#typed_state`
constructs the skeleton inside `Laws/Program/Typed/State.lean` from its roots and the
`Typed/Sources.lean` declaration. `#frame_rules` constructs checked theorems in
`Typed/Frames.lean`. Lake owns the dependencies and rebuilds both with the input changes;
the normal Laws/Test roots include them and their controls (`Test/Audit/`). A `Source.owner` row receives the entire structure
or every constructor argument. Its descendants are covered; a redundant row is refused. A `Source.each` row applies to a containment edge with one child type.
It states a hand predicate at each child the field holds, beside the child's own clause.
It covers nothing (decisions row 151 (a″): the scope store's registered finalizers).
A shared nested type still needs rows where another path reaches it outside that owner.
`TypedSources.lean` supplies the same ownership accounting to the source gate and the emitter.
Whole-owner frame rules require a new premise for every field update. The old
`TypedStateEmit.lean` file writer is retired.

The proof-ledger command reads obligation theorems and hole definitions, searches with
the supplied tactic, and checks the resulting theorem terms through `ProofGraph`.
`#obligation_proved X := term` supplies a proof of the exact statement directly; both routes
share the dependency checks and reject a remaining hole for a proved statement.
`#obligation_audit NS` compares complete binder lists and propositions against namesake laws;
argument adapters must already have checked evidence. Rendered counts are a report, not an input. Its missing/stale/wrong-proposition/ceiling controls are
in `Test/Audit/{ProofGraph,Obligations}.lean`. The concrete transition-preservation obligation
set still requires the typing-world instantiation; frame premises are not that proof count.

The scripts ledger retired `git:c67ff096:generated/schema-structural-assurance.tsv` on 2026-09-13.
Its 2,682 rows came from a 446-line producer that stored the SHA-256 of every Schema source.
It refused changed sources after the owner deferred its stamp on 2026-09-08.
The checking refactor retired its projected Lean module and three hand-frozen declaration censuses that day.
The derived projection guard (`tools/Effect4Gen/Check.lean`) and axiom gate now check constructor order, arity, owned names and receipts.
The retained Schema checks run on their inputs through `make check-sweep` and `check-ts`.
Row 39 retired the annotation and effectful-field harnesses and their `check-schema-host` gate.
The schema-ts group and host were deleted on 2026-10-20 (`git:38b94bdec:harness/schema-generation`).

The **evidence** column uses the words ruled on 2026-09-09 (DI-32).
*Proved* names a theorem.
*Reproduced* names a byte comparison against a fresh producer run.
*Tested* names a finite checker or host run over named inputs.
The former word *stamped* named a trace over producer inputs, with no claim about committed bytes.
It has no carrier since the labels left.
Every committed group carries *reproduced* evidence.

## Fragment predicates

The derived group includes `PrimFold` from `tools/Effect4Gen/Fold.lean`.
It generates `src/Effect4/Machine/Fold.lean` from `Effect4.Prim` in `src/Effect4/Machine/Frames.lean`.
Native code weights consume its algebra, fold, and uniqueness law.

The derived group includes `MlFold` from `tools/Effect4Gen/Fold.lean`.
It generates `src/OCaml5/Ml/Fold.lean` from the OCaml syntax of `src/OCaml5/Ml/Syntax.lean`.
The LCNF route's printer, checker, builtin uses and conformance reader are algebras of it.

The derived group includes `Fragments`, `FragmentLooped`, `FragmentRows`, and `FragmentLoopedRows` from `tools/Effect4Gen/Fragments.lean`.
They generate the existing fragment predicates from one classification table and the program family metadata.
The outputs are `src/Effect4/Program/Fragment.lean` and `src/Effect4/Laws/Program/Fragment{Looped,Rows,LoopedRows}.lean`.
The existing fold connectors remain in the Laws graph.
`docs/core/traversal-census.md` owns the classification rules and their limits.

## Build artifacts that are not committed

**Promoted projections.** Five committed tables are not cut by `make gen`; each has its own
producer. `generated/corpus-index.tsv` (`make corpus`, below) and `generated/row-types.tsv`
(`tools/Tools/RowTypes.lean`, which `make check-ts` runs before its target lane reads it) are
inputs. `generated/assignability.tsv` (`make gen-assignability`), `generated/row-citations.tsv`
(`make gen-row-citations`) and `generated/tsdiag-agreement.tsv` (`make gen-tsdiag`) are reports.
Each lane writes its fresh table under `.lake`.
No verdict reads the committed copy (owner, 2026-10-18: a pin that re-records on a spelling change is cut). The first four are in
`GENERATED_PATHS`, so `make check-gen` refuses a hand edit to them.

**The printed corpus.** `make corpus` runs `tools/Drivers/Corpus.lean` into `.lake/corpus`.
It writes 400 programs from Lean's seeded generator (`Test/Program/Gen.lean`) and the wire corpus.
Each program has `.ts` printer bytes, `.json` data retained by Lean's reader, and `.eff` canonical wire bytes.
`index.tsv` records Lean's `wellTyped` and `readable` verdicts per program.
`modules/<name>.ts` holds the unchecked module that `make check-ts` checks.
The reader, ingest and diagnostics steps of `make check-ts` read it.
The OCaml engine differential reads it inside `make check-ocaml`.
Its content key follows `Drivers.Corpus`, its source closure, tool identities and outputs.
Only the index is committed: `make corpus` installs it as `generated/corpus-index.tsv`.
`make check-gen` holds these bytes, with one row per program and its `wellTyped` and `readable` verdicts.
A typing or printer change names the affected programs in the diff (DI-60).
The generator previously pinned counts.

**The corpus on rc.112 and under tsgo 7. Retired 2026-10-18, deleted 2026-10-20** (owner:
"just retire them... we'll design better checks"; "retire the old truth modules"). The lane ran
the same 400 programs on the pinned runtime and compared Lean's types with the compiler's
(`git:fa7bdc304:scripts/check-corpus.py`). Its committed table went with it
(`git:fa7bdc304:harness/truth/corpus-results.tsv`). Its type oracle followed on 2026-10-20
(`git:8e93a284f:tools/target/corpus.ts`).

**Schema codec comparisons. Retired 2026-10-18,** with the schema-ts lane and its group: no
target runs them. The lane wrote a fresh TypeScript module into
the checker's work folder, which git ignores (`ts/eff/test/codec/.work/values.ts`, by
`tools/Drivers/CodecValues.lean`). It holds the public `Ty.encode` results for the
representative cases of `Test/Codegen/SchemaGenerationContract.lean`. It holds each case's typed
Schema as the code printer writes it (`Codegen.SchemaCode.ofTy`), and that Schema's persisted
document. tsgo 7 checks the module with `check.ts`. Then `check.ts` compares the results with
pinned rc.112 `Schema.toCodecJson` under the generated Schemas. It decodes and re-encodes them on
the host, and checks the rejected legacy Result/Cause shapes. It compares each generated Schema with rc.112's
revival of its document and with rc.112's own code of that revival (`toCodeDocument`). No codec
golden is committed. Finite host evidence, separate from the universal checked-boundary laws in
`Laws/Schema/Codec`.

**Conform outputs.** Source descriptions and conformance reports are build artifacts under
`.lake/conform/`; `scripts/check-conform.py` produces them freshly. The compiler profile's
OCaml is an inspected execution artifact, not a replacement for `ocaml/gen`.

**The truth and host-protocol lanes retired 2026-10-18, deleted 2026-10-20** (owner: "retire
the old truth modules"). The rc.112 truth differential's recorded results, tapes, build ledger,
release lane and scripts went first (`git:fa7bdc304:harness/truth`,
`git:fa7bdc304:scripts/check-truth.py`). Its runner and the print driver went next, with the
ingest's round-trip tool that ran them (`git:8e93a284f:harness/truth/run-truth.ts`,
`git:8e93a284f:ts/eff/ingest/fidelity/roundtrip.ts`). The target checker's two request kinds
that the lane sent went too. The keyed host lane's script and its service runner went with them
(`git:8e93a284f:scripts/check-host-protocol.py`, `git:8e93a284f:harness/truth/service`). The
keyed session's hand implementation went the same day (E8,
`git:98a29895b800556365a2edc9924f3ed12787b820:harness/truth/session`). Its generated projection
stays beside the prelude, in `ts/prelude/` (the next section).
`make gen` does not cut the truth corpus; `make gen-truth-corpus` writes it on demand (the
group `truth` above).

**The keyed session's working receipt** lived under an ignored `.work/` folder beside the

adapter in `git:98a29895b800556365a2edc9924f3ed12787b820:harness/truth/session/Session.lean` is explicit and separately version checked;
v2 never fills in missing keys from a replay's expected request.

## Host protocol projections

`ts/prelude/protocol.gen.ts` and `tape.schema.json` are deterministic committed
projections of `src/Effect4/Api/HostProtocol.lean`. The TypeScript adapter and the Lean JSON
driver both use the datum's record fields and transition table. The schema describes record
structure; `Envelope` remains responsible for the actual machine's row/request/completion
judgment. This schema is a tape schema, not a published content-address encoding
(DI-01/04). `make gen-host-protocol` writes both files, and `make check-gen-full` holds them
against drift.

Until 2026-10-18 the keyed host lane also regenerated and compared both files.
It emitted Eff fixtures accepted by program admission and their binding plans.
It ran the printed expressions on rc.112 and type-checked them.
It replayed recorded tapes in Lean with finite controls.
These covered missing, stale and duplicate keys, and wrong rows, requests or values.
They also covered reordered receipts and applications, zero application fuel, and empty public chunks.

The same lane performed the dogfood scenarios' scripts on their printed TypeScript modules
(decisions row 254). Lean wrote each script's fixture afresh into the work folder, and no
fixture of a scenario is committed. `Test/Dogfood/README.md`, section "The host runs", owns
what a host run compares. The lane pinned the digest of the four fixture families' recordings
(`git:8e93a284f:scripts/check-host-protocol.py`, `CASES_SHA256`).

The same lane performed the to-do's scripts on its emitted Effect service (decisions row 378
(20), `git:8e93a284f:harness/truth/service`). Lean decided each run's checks beside the
script's own run. The gates retired the lane on 2026-10-18, and its script and service runner
were deleted on 2026-10-20.

## Engine boundary

`ocaml/engine/api_engine.ml` is the LCNF projection of `Effect4.Api.run`/`replay`.
It uses the extern table `ocaml/engine/externs.txt` and hand-written prelude `ocaml/engine/tools/api_engine_prelude.ml`.
`ocaml/engine/tools/gen-check.sh` checks this boundary.
It checks that no fiber leaves the fiber table.
The generated modules build, their smoke passes, and the engine type-checks on its own.
The check also requires the current prelude in the generated file.
The recipe's first artifact, `ocaml/eff/eff_types.ml`, declares the program types alone.
Both engines open it.
The wire, codecs and engine instances share one OCaml program type, without a conversion or ordinal pin.

### LCNF interfaces

The LCNF recipe lists every public value as a root.
Coverage roots contribute implementation code only.
The retained engine prelude remains public.
`OCaml5.Lcnf.Gen.run` in `src/OCaml5/Lcnf/Gen.lean` stages implementations and exact public names.
`Lcnf_interface.generate` in `ocaml/gen/interface/lcnf_interface.ml` reads each fresh compiler typed tree.
It hides the whole representation of each package in the recipe's abstract list.
Nominal root ascriptions retain package names after proof erasure.
The OCaml compiler checks those ascriptions and each inferred interface.
`scripts/lib/lcnf_interfaces.py` publishes the family only after every artifact passes.
A previous interface cannot block its replacement because inference compiles a fresh copy.

A recipe artifact may list consumers, each a facade file and the roots it re-exports.
The artifact is one walk of its own roots and then all its consumers' roots, so they share every declaration they reach.
An artifact may compile that walk in two scopes (decision D1).
Its `closure` unit compiles every node its own roots reach, and `out` is a facade over it.
`out`'s interface is read off the closure's typed tree (`from`): it keeps the public and linkage roots and seals the packages.
Its `tests` unit compiles every node only the consumers reach, and it includes the closure.
Each consumer's facade includes the tests unit, and `Lcnf_interface` keeps its consumer's roots and the types they name.
So the LCNF route lowers each declaration once, and OCaml compiles it once.
The api artifact compiles its closure in `ocaml/gen/closure_gen.ml`, the package-private library `effect4_closure` of `effect4_gen`.
Its tests unit is `ocaml/engine/test/lanes/lanes_gen.ml`, a test library that nothing installs.

A recipe artifact may name the earlier artifacts it uses (`uses`, decisions row 428 (5)).
Its walk stops at each declaration a used artifact lowers and writes that artifact's binding by its module.
It spells the used artifact's own types through that module and declares none of them.
A root it lists that a used artifact lowers is bound by name, so its interfaces keep the root.
The used artifact's interface exports each binding its users link (`scripts/lib/lcnf_interfaces.py`, L8).
So a Lean declaration is lowered into one artifact.
The api artifact uses `ocaml/eff/eff_image.ml` and lowers none of the program codec's declarations.
The `api_gen` run prints how many declarations it links and compares its manifest with `eff_image`'s.
`lake exe lcnfgen --identity` compares closure manifests by declaration, code, target profile, type owner and builtin catalogue.
Run `python3 scripts/generate.py --only lcnf` to regenerate implementations, interfaces, and closure manifests.
Use `--output-dir DIR` to compare fresh outputs with the repository.
The interface controls run through `opam exec --switch=effect4 -- dune runtest --root ocaml gen/interface`.
